title: Apple GPU prefill 8x16x32 shared operand staging
question: When output ownership is held at one thread per output in an 8x16 tile, does cooperatively staging BK=32 input and weight tiles improve prefill projection timing?
hypothesis: Explicit staging will reduce source-requested X and W loads, and that reuse may repay the shared-memory accesses and barriers as M grows, especially for rotating weights.

control.ownership: One 128-thread group owns an 8x16 output rectangle; one thread owns one scalar output.
control.k_mapping: Each thread walks the full K dimension serially from device memory.

candidate.ownership: The same 128-thread group owns the same 8x16 output rectangle; one thread still owns one scalar output and one persistent FP32 accumulator.
candidate.cooperative_load: Each K phase stages 256 BF16 X values and 512 BF16 W values, with zero fill at M, N, and K tails.
candidate.edge_policy: All threads participate in both barriers; invalid operand coordinates write zero and invalid output owners skip only arithmetic and final storage.

unchanged: BF16 input, weight, bias, and output
FP32 accumulation and one final BF16 cast
row-major X[M,K], W[N,K], and Y[M,N] layouts
128 threads and 128 output owners per complete threadgroup tile
one enqueue per layer and one completion boundary per measured workload
no weight packing or quantization change

correctness.authority: tests/test_linear.mojo plus each benchmark implementation's untimed exact-unit-output gate
required_cases: Committed torch.nn.Linear short-prefill oracle M=3 K=33 N=5
Exact output tile M=8 K=32 N=16
Ragged tails M=9 K=33 N=17, including two K phases
Qwen KV width M=8 K=896 N=128
Existing decode, packed-QKV, direct-control, and two-output tests remain passing
correctness.gate: All 22 linear tests passed with device synchronization enabled before measurement.

workload_matrix.primary_interpretation_workload: The rotating packed-QKV curve, because hot repeated weights are exceptionally cache-favorable.

measurement_protocol.decisive_command: uv run --locked python benchmarks/run_linear_prefill.py --blocks 4 --experiment-id EXP-0008 --run-id EXP-0008-RUN-001 --tiled-comparison --recorded --output-dir <absolute-external-path>/EXP-0008-RUN-001
blocks: ascending workloads; direct control then tiled candidate
descending workloads; tiled candidate then direct control
descending workloads; tiled candidate then direct control
ascending workloads; direct control then tiled candidate
measurement_protocol.paired_statistic: Within each block and workload, tiled median divided by direct median; summarize the four ratios with their median and retain every ratio.
measurement_protocol.environment: Clean immutable commit, AC power, no reported thermal or performance warning, Apple GPU plus Metal runtime identity, and MODULAR_DEBUG unset.

classification_rule.material_improvement: Median paired ratio <= 0.95 and tiled faster in at least three of four blocks.
classification_rule.material_regression: Median paired ratio >= 1.05 and tiled slower in at least three of four blocks.
classification_rule.production_decision: None. This experiment isolates shared staging and does not select a public dispatch path.

nonclaims: No hardware cache, fabric, or DRAM traffic was measured.
Timing does not separately identify barrier, shared-access, instruction, occupancy, or compiler-code-generation cost.
The result does not establish that BK=32 is optimal or that all tiled matrix-multiplication mappings are slow.
No end-to-end prompt, model, or decoder throughput result.
No public dispatch threshold is selected.

decision.reason: The shared-staging candidate materially regressed every rotating packed-QKV row count by 65.46% to 74.53% in all four blocks despite lower source-requested operand loads.
decision.next_experiment: Hold BM=8, BN=16, and ownership fixed while screening BK=16, 64, and 128 on rotating workloads to test the shared-capacity versus barrier-count tradeoff before changing the arithmetic mapping.
